action_name: Composting food scraps instead of landfill
source_1_quote: 1 kg CH4 per dry ton materials * 23 kg CO2 per kg CH4 = 23 kg CO2 (well-managed compost) vs 207 kg CO2 (poorly managed).
source_2_quote: EPA research indicates that diverting food waste from landfill reduces the methane generation potential by 33%.
calculation_notes: Composting emits ~10-20% of landfill methane. Net savings ~700g/kg

action_name: Using LED instead of incandescent bulb

source_2_quote: A single 10-watt LED will save about 800 kWh over its lifetime. That single replacement will eliminate emissions of 1000 pounds of carbon dioxide.
calculation_notes: 60W incandescent vs 10W LED = 50W saved. At US grid 0.37kg/kWh = 18.5g/hour

action_name: Reusable shopping bag instead of plastic
source_1_name: UK Environment Agency 2011, Life cycle assessment of supermarket carrier bags
source_1_quote: No secondary use 2.082 40.28% secondary use 1.578 100% secondary use 0.830
source_2_name: UK Environment Agency 2011, Life cycle assessment of supermarket carrier bags
source_2_quote: The paper, LDPE, non-woven PP and cotton bags should be reused at least 3, 4, 11 and 131 times respectively
calculation_notes: per bag avoided: UK Environment Agency 2011 HDPE carrier bag, 0.830 kg CO2e per 82.14 bags (the reference flow) when every bag is reused as a bin liner = 10.1 g, rounded down to 10 g (1.578 kg = 19.2 g at the study's 40.28% bin-liner reuse). Break-even: at least 11 uses for non-woven PP and 131 for cotton (UK EA), 52 for cotton on climate change alone (Danish EPA 2018).
